name: SPS30 particulate matter sensor
description: Sensirion laser-scattering particulate matter sensor: mass concentration PM1.0/PM2.5/PM4.0/PM10 (0–1000 µg/m³), number concentration PM0.5–PM10 and typical particle size, a new reading every second, with a built-in fan. Runs on 4.5–5.5 V; I2C mode (SEL to GND) at address 0x69, 3.3 V logic levels. Sold as: Sensirion SPS30 with its 5-wire JST ZHR-5 cable (e.g. SparkFun SEN-15103), connector pins VDD, SDA, SCL, SEL, GND; no pull-up resistors on the sensor.
eli5: Sucks in air with a tiny fan and counts the dust and smoke particles in it with a laser, so you know how clean the air is.

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: Supply, 5 V ± 10 % (4.5–5.5 V); draws 55 mA (80 mA peak at fan start)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (pin 2, RX in UART mode). Open-drain, needs an external pull-up (10 kΩ) to 3.3 V; 5 V tolerant

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (pin 3, TX in UART mode). Open-drain, needs an external pull-up (10 kΩ) to 3.3 V; 5 V tolerant

pins.name: SEL
pins.description: Interface select: tie to GND (before power-up) for I2C; floating selects UART. Never connect to 5 V (max 4.0 V)

buildNotes: Power VDD from 5 V (4.5–5.5 V); the fan will not run reliably on 3.3 V. Budget 80 mA for the first 200 ms after a measurement starts.
SEL (pin 4) must be tied to GND before or at power-up to choose I2C; left floating the sensor talks UART instead. SEL is rated for 4.0 V max, so never tie it to 5 V.

SDA and SCL are open-drain and the sensor has no pull-ups: fit 10 kΩ resistors from SDA and from SCL to the board's 3.3 V (not 5 V, which would overdrive ESP32/Pico pins). The sensor accepts 3.3 V logic (VIH 2.31 V).
I2C is limited to 100 kHz and the datasheet recommends cables under 10 cm (use UART for longer runs).

Start Measurement is pointer 0x0010 with data 0x03 0x00 + CRC 0xAC (float output); poll 0x0202 for data ready, then read 60 bytes from 0x0300: ten big-endian floats, CRC-8 (poly 0x31, init 0xFF) after every 2 bytes.
Keep the metal housing floating: it is internally connected to GND.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from sps30 import SPS30

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
sensor = SPS30(i2c)
sensor.start()
while True:
    m = sensor.read()
    print('PM1.0=%.1f PM2.5=%.1f PM10=%.1f ug/m3 size=%.2f um' % (m['pm1_0'], m['pm2_5'], m['pm10'], m['typical_size']))
    time.sleep(1)
